records.people: Jean Boivin (Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada and Associate Deputy Finance Minister; Managing Director and Head of the BlackRock Investment Institute)
records.move: from Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada and Associate Deputy Finance Minister to BlackRock, which he joined in 2014, as Managing Director and Head of the BlackRock Investment Institute and BII's Global Head of Research
records.years: joined BlackRock in 2014 (the page gives no dates for the Bank of Canada post itself)
records.summary: BlackRock's own biography page for Jean Boivin states that before joining the firm in 2014 he was Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada and Associate Deputy Finance Minister, and that he is now Managing Director and Head of the BlackRock Investment Institute. The private side is BlackRock, an asset manager whose own page is the source; the page itself makes no statement about BlackRock's ownership or listing, and BlackRock is already carried on this map as a private financial party. The page gives no dates for the Bank of Canada post, so none is asserted here. Different person, firm and years from the Mark Carney / Goldman Sachs record the map already holds for Canada. OWNERSHIP, added by the curator on 17 November 2026: the BlackRock biography page names the employer and says nothing about who owns it, which on this row settles nothing by itself. BlackRock's own annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission under Commission File No. 001-42297, registers 'Common Stock, $.01 par value' under the symbol BLK on the New York Stock Exchange. That is the employer's own filing with its own regulator and it settles the private-financial leg in the document's own words.
records.quote: Prior to joining BlackRock in 2014, Dr. Boivin served as Deputy Governor of the Bank of Canada and Associate Deputy Finance Minister

records.people: Laura Maria Pires Alcântara Monteiro (Adviser to the Governor, Vice-Governor, Executive Administrator and Director of Banking Supervision at the Banco Nacional de Angola, 1990-2012)
records.move: from Vice-Governor and Executive Administrator of the Banco Nacional de Angola (1990-2012) to Independent Non-Executive Director of Banco de Fomento Angola (2023-2025), Vice-President of its board (2025) and proposed President of BFA's Remuneration Committee
records.years: 1990-2012 at the Banco Nacional de Angola; BFA board 2023-2025 and Vice-President 2025
records.summary: BFA's own published CVs of its proposed governing-body members state that Laura Maria Pires Alcântara Monteiro served at the Banco Nacional de Angola as Adviser to the Governor, Vice-Governor, Executive Administrator, Director of Banking Supervision, Director of Studies and Statistics and head of the Balance of Payments department between 1990 and 2012, and that she was an Independent Non-Executive Director of BFA in 2023-2025, Vice-President of its board in 2025 and is proposed as President of BFA's Remuneration Committee; the same CV records that she holds 2,409 ordinary shares in BFA. The private side is Banco de Fomento Angola, whose ownership is stated as mixed by a second source named in this record: Ver Angola, 'BPI chega a acordo com Grupo Carrinho para venda de participação no BFA', says BFA's principal shareholders were Unitel ('controlada pelo Estado') with 36.90 per cent and BPI ('detido pelo grupo espanhol Caixabank') with 33.35 per cent, with 14.75 per cent sold on the stock exchange. Mixed ownership is therefore stated on the face of this record, not assumed.
records.source_title: Curricula of the proposed members of BFA's governing bodies (CVs órgãos BFA), Banco de Fomento Angola

The concurrent sovereign-fund seat is a state body and is recorded here only as context.

blanks.read: ZMB: Standard Chartered Bank Zambia Plc's own 'Board of Directors' page (sc.com/zm/about-us/board-of-directors) read in full. All seven directors are listed with career histories — Irene Lombe Chibesakunda (Chair, appointed 1 October 2023), Sonny Zulu (MD and CEO), Kelvin Bwalya (CFO, 1 April 2020), Mainga Mukando, Christopher Egberink (13 December 2022), Misozi Hope Masengu (1 November 2024) and David Ngandu — and NONE of them names the Bank of Zambia. The only public-sector employers named are the Zambia Revenue Authority, the Ministry of Finance and National Planning and the Ministry of Gender. The page also makes no statement about Standard Chartered's own ownership or listing. Vein for Zambia: the foreign-owned commercial banks' board pages are the right shape but this one is clean; Access Bank Zambia's 'Board & Management Team' page (zambia.accessbankplc.com/about-us/board-management-team) and Zambia Industrial Commercial Bank (zicb.co.zm) were returned by search and NOT opened — try those next.

BRB: the Central Bank of Barbados's own past-governor page for Mr Winston Cox (centralbank.org.bb/leadership/past-governors/mr-winston-cox) read in full. It gives his whole career — Ministry of Health to 1974, the Bank's own Research Department 1974-1987 rising to Deputy Director and adviser to the Governor, Ministry of Finance and Planning from 1987, chairman of Barbados Sugar Industries Ltd 1991-1992, UNDP fiscal adviser to Grenada 1992-1994, World Bank alternate executive director from 1994, Governor September 1997 to April 1999, then about a year as an IMF adviser, Deputy Secretary-General of the Commonwealth Secretariat September 2000 to June 2006, and alternate executive director at the Inter-American Development Bank. There is no private bank or financial firm anywhere in it: his single private-sector post is a sugar company, which is not financial. Vein for Barbados: this past-governors series is one page per governor and is the right route, but Cox's own page closes him. Dr Kurleigh King's page (centralbank.org.bb/leadership/past-governors/dr-kurleigh-king) was returned by search and NOT opened, and pages for Marion Williams, Delisle Worrell and Cleviston Haynes should exist on the same path.

UZB: two Central Bank of Uzbekistan leadership pages read in full — cbu.uz/en/about/management/74124/ (Abror Mirzo Olimov, Deputy Chairman and Member of the Board, in post since 2024) and cbu.uz/en/about/management/74125/ (Timur Ishmetov, Chairman, in post since 2024). The CBU's published career table for a board member carries only three fields — place of work and position, years of banking experience (10 for Olimov, 19 for Ishmetov) and time in current position — plus education. It does not list prior employers at all, so no commercial or private bank can be read off it, for any board member, on any of these pages. Vein closed: the CBU's own leadership pages cannot settle a career move however many of them are opened. A different route is needed for Uzbekistan — the commercial banks' own management pages, e.g. ipotekabank.uz/en/about/management/ (an individual officer bio page was returned by search and not opened), noting that Ipoteka Bank was state-owned before its sale, so for that employer the years decide the ownership.

PSE: two Palestine Monetary Authority board biography URLs were opened and NEITHER served its biography — pma.ps/About-PMA/Board-of-Directors/Mr-Azzam-Shawwa and pma.ps/en/AboutPMA/BoardofDirectors/DrFouadHamdiShabanBseiso both returned only the site's homepage metadata shell (title, description, social tags) with no person's name, post or employer in the body. This is the quiet-failure shape the brief warns about: a 200 carrying the wrong document. The biographies are rendered client-side. Palestine has NOT actually been tested. Search also returned pma.ps/AboutPMA/BoardofDirectors (the index), pma.ps/MrMohammad-Manasrah, pma.ps/en/About-PMA/Board-of-Directors/MrMajdi-ALhasan, islamicbank.ps/en/About%20/corporate-governance/board and bop.ps/en/about/corporate-governance/board-responsibilities — the two commercial banks' own governance pages are the better next route, since a Palestinian bank's annual report carries a director's CV and the shareholder table in one document.

AZE (a second candidate, logged not filed): pasha-life.az/en/about/r-hb-rlik/direktorlar-surasi/calal-qasimov/ read in full. It lists Calal Qasimov's career as 1st Deputy CEO of PASHA Holding, Chairman of the Kapital Bank Supervisory Board, CEO of UNIBANK and CEO/Chairman of the Management Board of Bank of Baku, with no years for any of them, and it does not mention the Central Bank of Azerbaijan anywhere. No central bank leg, so it is not a career move for this row at all. Also noted for the next round: the CBA's own leadership pages at cbar.az/organization/staff/detail/<n> are one dated biography per board member or adviser and DO carry prior private employers in the Azerbaijani text — detail/68 converted — while details 57, 65, 70 were returned by search and not opened.

TZA: search only; no document opened, so Tanzania has not been tested. The leads the search returned and did not open: bot.go.tz/Board (the Bank of Tanzania's own board page) and bot.go.tz/Governors ('Present and Past Governors and Deputy Governors'), which together give the names to check; and on the private side thecitizen.co.tz article 'Mchechu appointed board chairman Bank of Africa' (Bank of Africa Tanzania Limited, part of the Bank of Africa / BMCE group) plus the CRDB Bank and NMB Bank governance reports. The leads returned and not opened: eldinero.com.do/225160/como-steven-puig-se-convierte-en-presidente-del-banco-bhd (Steven Puig becoming president of Banco BHD) and secmca.org's individual CV PDF for Héctor Valdez Albizu, which is the same CV series (secmca.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/<name>-<bank>.pdf) that produced the filed Honduras record — that series covers every Central American and Dominican central bank chief and is the cheapest untried route for DOM, HND and SLV at once.

SUR: one Dutch-language search run, no document opened. Leads returned and not opened: www3.cbvs.sr/en/37-about-cbvs/546-directory (the Centrale Bank van Suriname's own directory of its directors) and srherald.com/suriname/2020/02/21/maurice-roemer-wordt-beedigd-als-nieuwe-governor (the swearing-in of Governor Maurice Roemer, who came from the commercial banking side). The existing Suriname record rests on Wikipedia, so almost any primary CV here would also be an upgrade in source quality.

MOZ: not searched this round. Recorded because the route is known and cheap: the existing Mozambique record came from an individual CV PDF on millenniumbim.co.mz (millenniumbim.co.mz/media/5100/cv-<name>.pdf), and that is a numbered series of unlinked individual CV PDFs for the bank's officers — the same shape as the BFA document that produced three Angola records this round. Neighbouring media ids on that host are the obvious next pull.

Fourteen of the 28 assigned places were not searched at all and are untested on this row: BIH, COD, COM, GAB, GMB, HND, IRQ, KGZ, MAC, MDV, SLV, TCD. (BIH carries a particular caution: the map's existing BIH record is sourced to cbbh.ba/Content/Read/119, the CBBH Governing Board page, so another board member taken off that same page would be a URL match and a duplicate under the brief's test — a different document is needed.) For IRQ the existing record came from api.idb.iq's annual report PDF, i.e. an Iraqi private bank's own annual report, which is a repeatable series. Budget went instead to the places where a single document settled career and ownership together.
